B: Hiya! Lee, isn't it? I'm Lisa.
A: Yeah. All right.
B: You look shattered, bless you. Sorry, that's rude, my husband Dean looks like that every night when he gets in.
A: I'm fine. Long day. Been on the M62 since seven.
B: Oh, I feel that. The A14's my one. Lorries everywhere 'cause of the port. What do you do?
A: Sales rep. Builders' merchants.
B: Oh, Dean's an electrician, self-employed. He's always moaning about the merchants, prices going up.
A: Everyone moans about the prices. Then they buy it anyway.
B: Ha! That's true, he does. Where are you, then?
A: Wakefield. You?
B: Ipswich. Do you have kids? I think I spotted a school jumper on your settee.
A: Yeah, Kieran. Eleven. Just started secondary.
B: Oh, bless him. Is he settling in?
A: Says it's fine. Martin reckons that's normal till Christmas.
B: Martin's lovely, isn't he? He reminds me of my dad. Mine's Callum, he's twenty-four, moved to Norwich. I still miss him, if I'm honest. You blink and they're gone.
A: Yeah. Me mum says the same about me. I'm ten minutes away, she still says it.
B: Ha! Do you see a lot of her?
A: All the time. She does Kieran's school pickups. Sunday dinner at hers most weeks.
B: Oh, that's lovely. You look after her, though, don't you? Mine's started getting a bit forgetful, so I'm round a lot more.
A: She's getting on a bit. I try. I probably lean on her more than I should, to be fair.
B: I think everyone does. That's what mums are for, isn't it. Erm, do you go away much? Holidays?
A: Tenerife, Lanzarote. Book it on me phone at work when it's quiet. Nearly missed the flight twice.
B: No! I'm exactly the same! Late deals, every time. We did Lanzarote last year, Puerto del Carmen.
A: Been there. It's all right. Does the job.
B: Does the job, that's it! Sun, pool, chips. Dean wants to go back, I said we'll see, which means yes.
A: What's your Friday tea, then? Chippy?
B: Chinese, usually. We've got the calendar on the wall from them, that's how loyal we are.
A: Saw that in your photo. Thought it were a nice touch.
